X1.name: Role Definition and Priority Clarification
X1.definition: Management explicitly defines role priorities and confirms project work takes precedence over routine tasks.
X1.pattern: IF management documents confirm project work is prioritized over routine tasks and this is communicated to the employee THEN support X1

X2.name: Client-Facing Escalation Work
X2.definition: Employee is assigned complex, client-facing escalation work with regulatory sensitivity.
X2.pattern: IF management records describe the employee's role as involving direct client engagement on complex, regulatory-sensitive matters THEN support X2

X3.name: Environment Switching Without Warning
X3.definition: Employee performs environment switching as part of assigned work without prior knowledge of adverse effects.
X3.pattern: IF the employee switches environments for work purposes without prior knowledge of adverse effects and no warning is given THEN support X3
required_elements: no prior knowledge of adverse effects

X4.name: Management Endorsement of Work Practices
X4.definition: Management repeatedly endorses the employee's work practices without raising concerns.
X4.pattern: IF management repeatedly endorses the employee's work practices and does not raise concerns or provide corrective instructions THEN support X4

X5.name: Excessive Workload Without Adjustment
X5.definition: Employee experiences excessive workload due to assigned priorities without management intervention.
X5.pattern: IF the employee experiences excessive workload due to assigned priorities and management does not intervene THEN support X5

DIRECT_X.definition: Case directly supports the employee's claims based on management's documented role definitions and endorsements.

CONTRASTIVE.definition: Case presents conflicting evidence that contradicts the employee's claims or management's documented role definitions.

REMEDY.definition: Case suggests potential remedies or corrective actions based on the documented role definitions and endorsements.

IRRELEVANT.definition: Case does not provide relevant evidence to support or contradict the employee's claims or management's documented role definitions.

hard_rules: Evidence must be directly tied to management's documented role definitions and endorsements.
Conflicting evidence must be explicitly addressed in the case summary.
Remedies must be based on the documented role definitions and endorsements.
Irrelevant evidence must be excluded from the case summary.

X1.name: Role Change Leading to Disciplinary Action
X1.definition: Disciplinary action initiated after a role change without corresponding conduct changes
X1.pattern: IF a role change occurs and disciplinary action is initiated solely based on activities from the prior role THEN support X1

X2.name: Inconsistent Role Expectations
X2.definition: Disciplinary process applies junior role standards to senior role activities
X2.pattern: IF disciplinary action is based on applying junior role standards to senior role activities THEN support X2

X3.name: Lack of Contemporaneous Instruction
X3.definition: Disciplinary action without prior instructions or guidance
X3.pattern: IF disciplinary action is taken without prior instructions or guidance on role changes THEN support X3

X4.name: Retrospective Application of Standards
X4.definition: Disciplinary action based on retrospective application of new role standards
X4.pattern: IF disciplinary action is based on retrospectively applying new role standards to past activities THEN support X4

X5.name: System Data Misinterpretation
X5.definition: Disciplinary action relying on misinterpreted system data
X5.pattern: IF disciplinary action relies on system data without considering role differences THEN support X5

X6.name: Managerial Encouragement of Role Change
X6.definition: Role change encouraged by manager without demotion implications
X6.pattern: IF a role change is encouraged by a manager and not communicated as a demotion THEN support X6

X7.name: Disciplinary Action Based on Role Change Alone
X7.definition: Disciplinary action initiated solely due to role change
X7.pattern: IF disciplinary action is initiated solely due to a role change without any conduct changes THEN support X7

DIRECT_X.definition: Case directly supports the claim of unfair disciplinary action due to role change

CONTRASTIVE.definition: Case provides evidence against the claim of unfair disciplinary action

REMEDY.definition: Case suggests a remedy or corrective action for the unfair disciplinary process

IRRELEVANT.definition: Case does not relate to the claim of unfair disciplinary action due to role change

hard_rules: Evidence must directly relate to the role change and disciplinary action
Disciplinary action must be based on activities from the prior role
No conduct changes should be noted for the claim to be valid
Role change must be encouraged or supported by management

X1.name: Lack of Prior Notice of Disciplinary Meeting
X1.definition: Failure to provide adequate notice of a disciplinary meeting, including agenda and purpose.
X1.pattern: IF a meeting is scheduled without prior notice of its disciplinary nature THEN support X1
required_elements: no prior notice of disciplinary nature

X2.name: First Presentation of Allegations
X2.definition: Allegations are raised for the first time during a disciplinary meeting without prior communication.
X2.pattern: IF allegations are presented for the first time during a meeting THEN support X2

X3.name: Inconsistent Explanations
X3.definition: Investigators misinterpret explanations as inconsistent when they are actually consistent.
X3.pattern: IF investigators claim explanations are inconsistent when they are consistent THEN support X3

X4.name: Lack of Written Instructions
X4.definition: No written instructions were provided regarding working practices that later became a disciplinary issue.
X4.pattern: IF no written instructions were given for working practices THEN support X4

X5.name: Mischaracterization of System Effects
X5.definition: System effects were mischaracterized as 'crashes' without prior communication of this terminology.
X5.pattern: IF system effects are mischaracterized as 'crashes' without prior notice THEN support X5

DIRECT_X.definition: Direct evidence supporting a claim of procedural unfairness or lack of due process.

CONTRASTIVE.definition: Evidence that contradicts or undermines a claim of procedural unfairness.

REMEDY.definition: Evidence suggesting a potential remedy or corrective action.

IRRELEVANT.definition: Evidence that does not support or contradict any claim of procedural unfairness.

hard_rules: Evidence must be directly related to the disciplinary process or meeting.
Contradictory evidence must be explicitly addressed.
Misinterpretations by investigators must be clearly identified.
Written instructions must be explicitly mentioned or absent.

X1.name: Reassurance Without Qualification
X1.definition: Unqualified reassurance given during a meeting indicating no further action will be taken.
X1.pattern: IF a meeting occurs where unqualified reassurance is given without indication of further action THEN support X1
positive_indicators: ok, it is fine, do not worry

X2.name: Reliance on Reassurance
X2.definition: Reliance on reassurance leading to normal continuation of duties without preparation for disciplinary action.
X2.pattern: IF reassurance is given and relied upon to continue duties normally without preparation THEN support X2

X3.name: Subsequent Conduct Indicating Closure
X3.definition: Subsequent conduct by management indicating the matter is closed.
X3.pattern: IF management's subsequent conduct indicates the matter is closed THEN support X3

X4.name: Contemporaneous Internal Correspondence
X4.definition: Internal correspondence reinforcing the understanding that the matter is closed.
X4.pattern: IF contemporaneous internal correspondence reinforces the understanding that the matter is closed THEN support X4

X5.name: Objective Reasonableness of Conclusion
X5.definition: Objective reasonableness of concluding the matter is closed based on reassurance and subsequent conduct.
X5.pattern: IF reassurance and subsequent conduct objectively support the conclusion that the matter is closed THEN support X5
positive_indicators: objectively reasonable to conclude matter closed
no basis to anticipate disciplinary action

DIRECT_X.definition: Direct evidence supporting the claim of reassurance, reliance, and subsequent conduct indicating closure of the matter.

CONTRASTIVE.definition: Evidence that contradicts the claim of reassurance, reliance, and subsequent conduct indicating closure of the matter.

REMEDY.definition: Evidence suggesting a remedy or action based on the reassurance, reliance, and subsequent conduct.

IRRELEVANT.definition: Evidence that does not pertain to the claim of reassurance, reliance, and subsequent conduct indicating closure of the matter.

hard_rules: Evidence must directly support or contradict the claim of reassurance, reliance, and subsequent conduct.
Objective reasonableness of the conclusion must be assessable from the evidence.
Contemporaneous internal correspondence must reinforce the understanding of matter closure.
Subsequent conduct by management must be consistent with the matter being closed.

X1.name: Failure to Distinguish Queue Time
X1.definition: The analysis does not differentiate between crashes occurring during designated queue time and those occurring outside it.
X1.pattern: IF the analysis does not separate crashes by queue time status THEN support X1
required_elements: crashes not distinguished by queue time
positive_indicators: crashes not correlated with queue time

X2.name: Absence of Verifiable Data
X2.definition: The analysis relies on high-level summary figures without providing underlying system logs.
X2.pattern: IF the analysis lacks underlying system logs and relies on summary figures THEN support X2

X3.name: Misinterpretation of Crash Figures
X3.definition: The analysis misinterprets crash figures as inherently probative without context.
X3.pattern: IF the analysis treats crash figures as probative without context THEN support X3

X4.name: Inconsistent Inferences
X4.definition: The analysis draws internally inconsistent inferences from the data.
X4.pattern: IF the analysis draws inferences that contradict other evidence THEN support X4

X5.name: Lack of Operational Impact Evidence
X5.definition: The analysis lacks evidence of operational impact linked to the alleged crashes.
X5.pattern: IF the analysis lacks evidence of operational impact from crashes THEN support X5

X6.name: Unsupported Conclusions
X6.definition: The analysis draws conclusions without sufficient supporting evidence.
X6.pattern: IF the conclusions are drawn without sufficient evidence THEN support X6

X7.name: Incompatible Work Instructions
X7.definition: The analysis ignores instructions that the work method was known and not prohibited.
X7.pattern: IF the analysis ignores known work instructions THEN support X7

DIRECT_X.definition: The case directly supports one or more of the atomic tests.

CONTRASTIVE.definition: The case contrasts with one or more of the atomic tests.

REMEDY.definition: The case suggests a remedy or corrective action based on the atomic tests.

IRRELEVANT.definition: The case does not relate to any of the atomic tests.

hard_rules: If a case supports at least one atomic test, it cannot be classified as IRRELEVANT.
If a case contradicts the evidence required for an atomic test, it must be classified as CONTRASTIVE.
If a case suggests a remedy based on the atomic tests, it must be classified as REMEDY.
If a case does not relate to any of the atomic tests, it must be classified as IRRELEVANT.

X1.name: Inadequate Notice for Disciplinary Hearing
X1.definition: Insufficient time provided to prepare for a disciplinary hearing, impacting the ability to gather evidence and secure representation.
X1.pattern: IF the notice period for a disciplinary hearing is less than three days AND it materially limits preparation AND no prior notification was given THEN support X1
required_elements: notice period less than three days

X2.name: Misrepresentation of Hearing Invitation
X2.definition: Incorrect assertion about the timing of the disciplinary hearing invitation.
X2.pattern: IF the respondent claims a prior invitation date AND the actual invitation date is later AND there is no prior notification THEN support X2

X3.name: Defence Submission Before Hearing
X3.definition: Submission of a written defence before the disciplinary hearing to ensure fair consideration.
X3.pattern: IF a written defence is submitted before the hearing AND it outlines core points AND relevant evidence is included THEN support X3

X4.name: Defence Not Properly Engaged
X4.definition: Failure to properly address the substance of the defence in the disciplinary outcome.
X4.pattern: IF the defence is submitted in good faith AND the disciplinary outcome does not address the substance of the points AND evidence raised THEN support X4

X5.name: Objective Evidence of Work Ethic
X5.definition: Presentation of objective evidence demonstrating a strong work ethic and commitment to responsibilities.
X5.pattern: IF objective evidence of work ethic is presented AND it demonstrates commitment to responsibilities AND it is relevant to the allegations THEN support X5

DIRECT_X.definition: Directly supports the claim of procedural prejudice in the disciplinary process.

CONTRASTIVE.definition: Provides evidence that contradicts the claim of procedural prejudice.

REMEDY.definition: Suggests a potential remedy or corrective action for the procedural prejudice.

IRRELEVANT.definition: Does not relate to the claim of procedural prejudice in the disciplinary process.

hard_rules: If a test is supported, it must be clearly indicated in the summary.
Evidence must be explicitly mentioned to support or contradict the claim.
The summary must provide a clear reasoning_for_index for the classification.
If no evidence is provided, the case must be classified as IRRELEVANT.

X1.name: Insufficient Notice of Hearing
X1.definition: Failure to provide adequate notice of a disciplinary hearing as per the Respondent’s own procedure.
X1.pattern: IF the notice period is less than three days and does not allow for meaningful preparation THEN support X1
required_elements: notice period less than three days
failure to provide sufficient information about allegations

X2.name: Failure to Provide Relevant Documents
X2.definition: Failure to provide relevant documents in advance of the hearing as required by the Respondent’s procedure.
X2.pattern: IF relevant documents are not provided in advance and are necessary for preparation THEN support X2
required_elements: documents are relevant to the case

X3.name: Failure to Adjourn Hearing for Further Investigation
X3.definition: Failure to adjourn the hearing to investigate new and material points raised during the hearing.
X3.pattern: IF new and material points are raised during the hearing and the hearing is not adjourned THEN support X3

X4.name: Inadequate Opportunity to Be Accompanied
X4.definition: Failure to provide a fair opportunity to be accompanied as per the Respondent’s procedure.
X4.pattern: IF the notice period is insufficient to arrange accompaniment and no accommodation is offered THEN support X4
required_elements: procedure requires opportunity to be accompanied

DIRECT_X.definition: The case directly supports a claim of procedural unfairness based on the Respondent’s failure to comply with its own disciplinary procedure.

CONTRASTIVE.definition: The case highlights procedural deficiencies but does not directly support a claim of unfairness.

REMEDY.definition: The case suggests a specific remedy or corrective action to address the procedural deficiencies.

IRRELEVANT.definition: The case does not relate to procedural unfairness or the Respondent’s disciplinary procedure.

hard_rules: At least one test must be supported to classify as DIRECT_X
Evidence must be specific to the Respondent’s disciplinary procedure
General complaints about fairness without specific procedural violations do not count
The case must involve a disciplinary hearing to be relevant

X1.name: Premature Disclosure of Allegations
X1.definition: Communication of contested allegations as established facts during an ongoing appeal
X1.pattern: IF an allegation is communicated as fact during an ongoing appeal THEN support X1

X2.name: Failure to Address Internal Dissemination
X2.definition: No action taken to address or investigate internal dissemination of allegations
X2.pattern: IF no steps are taken to address internal dissemination of allegations during appeal THEN support X2

X3.name: Predetermination Evidence
X3.definition: Evidence suggesting the appeal outcome was predetermined
X3.pattern: IF management communicates allegations as fact during appeal THEN support X3

X4.name: Breach of Confidentiality
X4.definition: Unauthorized disclosure of confidential and personal information
X4.pattern: IF confidential information is disclosed to unauthorized parties THEN support X4

X5.name: Adverse Consequences of Disclosure
X5.definition: Material and adverse consequences resulting from the disclosure
X5.pattern: IF disclosure leads to adverse professional consequences THEN support X5

X6.name: Contextual Evidence of Procedural Failures
X6.definition: Evidence of broader procedural failures and inconsistencies
X6.pattern: IF cumulative procedural failures are identified THEN support X6

X7.name: Lack of Fair and Open-Minded Process
X7.definition: Evidence suggesting the disciplinary process was not fair or open-minded
X7.pattern: IF evidence supports an inference of unfair process THEN support X7

DIRECT_X.definition: Direct evidence supporting the core factual/legal signals in X

CONTRASTIVE.definition: Evidence that contrasts or undermines the core factual/legal signals in X

REMEDY.definition: Evidence suggesting a remedy or corrective action is needed

IRRELEVANT.definition: Evidence that does not support or contrast the core factual/legal signals in X

hard_rules: Evidence must be directly related to the appeal process to support DIRECT_X
Contrastive evidence must directly undermine the core factual/legal signals in X
Remedy evidence must suggest a specific corrective action
Irrelevant evidence must not be related to the appeal process or core factual/legal signals in X

X1.name: Factual Basis for Allegations
X1.definition: Test for whether the appeal challenges the factual basis of the allegations made against the appellant.
X1.pattern: IF the appeal explicitly denies the factual basis of allegations and provides evidence to contradict them THEN support X1

X2.name: Proportionality of Dismissal
X2.definition: Test for whether the appeal argues that the dismissal was disproportionate to the alleged misconduct.
X2.pattern: IF the appeal argues that dismissal was disproportionate and provides comparative evidence or contextual factors THEN support X2

X3.name: Management Expectations
X3.definition: Test for whether the appeal argues that the dismissal was based on a misunderstanding or misapplication of management expectations.
X3.pattern: IF the appeal argues that management expectations were misunderstood or misapplied and provides evidence of instructions or role definitions THEN support X3

X4.name: Lack of Corrective Guidance
X4.definition: Test for whether the appeal argues that no corrective guidance or warnings were provided before dismissal.
X4.pattern: IF the appeal argues that no corrective guidance or warnings were provided and provides evidence of lack of communication THEN support X4
positive_indicators: no such clarification, warning, or corrective guidance
excludes: general claims of lack of communication

X5.name: Comparator Evidence
X5.definition: Test for whether the appeal uses comparator evidence to challenge the consistency of the disciplinary decision.
X5.pattern: IF the appeal provides comparator evidence showing inconsistent treatment of similar cases THEN support X5
positive_indicators: colleague holding the same corporate title
resolved one ticket over an entire year

DIRECT_X.definition: The case directly supports the appeal's arguments with clear evidence and logical reasoning.

CONTRASTIVE.definition: The case contrasts the appeal's arguments with other evidence or standards to highlight inconsistencies.

REMEDY.definition: The case suggests a specific remedy or corrective action based on the appeal's arguments.

IRRELEVANT.definition: The case does not provide relevant evidence or reasoning to support the appeal's arguments.

hard_rules: Evidence must be specific and falsifiable to support any test.
General claims without specific evidence do not count towards any test.
Comparator evidence must involve similar roles and circumstances to be valid.
Lack of corrective guidance must be explicitly stated and supported by evidence.

X1.name: Failure to Provide Timely Resolution
X1.definition: The respondent failed to provide a timely resolution to the appeal despite repeated requests and knowledge of the appellant's financial pressure.
X1.pattern: IF the respondent fails to provide a timely resolution to the appeal despite repeated requests and knowledge of the appellant's financial pressure THEN support X1
excludes: general delay without context of financial pressure

X2.name: Lack of Genuine Reconsideration
X2.definition: The appeal outcome did not involve a genuine or open-minded reconsideration of the decision to dismiss.
X2.pattern: IF the appeal outcome fails to engage with central logical flaws and does not reconsider the decision to dismiss THEN support X2
required_elements: failure to engage with central logical flaw
positive_indicators: failed to engage with central logical flaw

X3.name: Reliance on Unsupported Oral Recall
X3.definition: The appeal outcome relied on an unsupported oral recall without contemporaneous documentation.
X3.pattern: IF the appeal outcome relies on an unsupported oral recall without contemporaneous documentation THEN support X3
positive_indicators: oral recall provided by team leader
excludes: general mention of oral evidence without context

X4.name: Inconsistent and Unreasonable Reasoning
X4.definition: The appeal outcome contained inconsistent and unreasonable reasoning regarding the appellant's conduct.
X4.pattern: IF the appeal outcome contains inconsistent and unreasonable reasoning regarding the appellant's conduct THEN support X4

X5.name: Failure to Reconcile Conclusions with Data
X5.definition: The appeal outcome failed to reconcile its conclusions with the respondent's own data.
X5.pattern: IF the appeal outcome fails to reconcile its conclusions with the respondent's own data THEN support X5
required_elements: failure to engage with performance metrics
lack of investigation into comparator evidence
positive_indicators: failed to engage with performance metrics
lack of investigation into comparator evidence
excludes: general mention of data without context

DIRECT_X.definition: The appeal outcome demonstrates significant flaws and failures that directly impact the fairness of the dismissal.

CONTRASTIVE.definition: The appeal outcome contains elements that contrast with the appellant's evidence and arguments.

REMEDY.definition: The appeal outcome requires remedial action due to its flaws and failures.

IRRELEVANT.definition: The appeal outcome does not demonstrate significant flaws or failures that impact the fairness of the dismissal.

hard_rules: Evidence of financial pressure must be explicitly mentioned to support X1.
Failure to engage with central logical flaws must be explicitly mentioned to support X2.
Reliance on unsupported oral recall must be explicitly mentioned to support X3.
Inconsistent and unreasonable reasoning must be explicitly mentioned to support X4.
Failure to reconcile conclusions with data must be explicitly mentioned to support X5.
